bb7075d85f3fa7f50bb58ed5e7818d07dd59f41f.summary:
The game is built — a single self-contained `index.html` (no dependencies beyond a Google Fonts link for the chunky "Press Start 2P" arcade font). Open it in a browser to play.

Everything from the plan is in:

- **Core mechanics** — 20×20 grid, 24px chunky cells, queued input (up to 2 buffered turns so fast double-taps register), no instant 180° reversals, and the classic tail-cell exception so moving into the spot your tail is vacating doesn't kill you.
- **Neon trails** — the canvas clears with a translucent fill each frame instead of a full wipe, so the glowing snake leaves fading light trails; head is cyan, body is green with shadow-blur glow, food is a pulsing pink diamond.
- **Speed ramp** — starts at 150ms per move, shaves 4ms per food eaten, capped at 55ms.
- **Screen shake** — on crash the canvas jitters with decaying magnitude for ~420ms while the snake flashes red/white, then the GAME OVER screen drops in.
- **Score + persistence** — HUD shows SCORE and HI-SCORE; the high score survives refreshes via `localStorage` (wrapped in try/catch so it degrades gracefully if storage is blocked), with a blinking "★ NEW HI-SCORE ★" callout when you beat it.
- **Start screen** — pulsing NEON SNAKE title, blinking "▶ INSERT COIN ◀" button, a "© 2026 VIBEHUB AMUSEMENTS" credit line, plus CRT scanlines over the whole page and a cyan glowing cabinet frame.
- **Controls** — arrows and WASD both work; any movement key, Space, Enter, or the coin button starts a game, and Space/Enter/click restarts from game over.

As a bonus there are tiny WebAudio chiptune beeps (coin-up jingle, eat blips that rise in pitch, a descending crash sound) and a particle burst when you eat — all generated in code, no assets needed.

65d94810f6850e7e4cbf05ca3c9b8f797806cad5.summary:
Everything checks out. The implementation is complete:

**Power-ups** — a spawner drops one item at a time onto a free cell every 6–13 seconds, and it sits on the board for 9 seconds (blinking for the last 2.5 before vanishing):
- **Yuzu berry** (glowing yellow orb with a little green leaf, bobbing gently): slows the game tick to 1.8× its normal interval for 6 seconds — a breather when the snake gets fast.
- **Ghost star** (pulsing white five-point star with cyan glow): for 6 seconds, self-collision is skipped in the step logic so you can pass straight through your own body; walls still kill you. While ghosted, the snake renders translucent white/cyan with a shimmering flicker so you can see the mode is active.

**Visible countdowns** — a new center slot in the HUD shows a bordered badge per active effect (`● SLOW-MO 4.2` in yellow, `★ GHOST 3.1` in cyan/white), ticking down in tenths of a second and blinking during the final 1.5 seconds. Both can run at once.

**Pause** — pressing P during play swaps to a `paused` state with a proper PAUSED overlay (big pulsing cyan title, a legend explaining both power-ups, and a blinking "PRESS P TO RESUME"; clicking the overlay also resumes). While paused the canvas stops rendering so the frame freezes under the overlay, and because effect timers, power-up lifetimes, and the spawn clock only advance in the `playing` state, pausing freezes every countdown exactly where it was.

The start screen hints were updated to mention P-to-pause and the two power-ups. Everything stays in the single self-contained `index.html` with no external assets.

The merge is done — the game is now a single self-contained `index.html` with three render modes sharing one game engine, one hi-score, and all the arcade juice.

What changed:

- **Mode select on the INSERT COIN screen**: three neon buttons (1·2D / 2·2.5D / 3·3D), and keys **1/2/3 switch the view at any time** — even mid-game, since all three modes render the same live game state. The last-used mode persists in `localStorage` (`neonSnakeMode`), and the hi-score stays a single shared key across all views. A small "VIEW 2.5D"-style tag sits in the frame corner so you always know which mode you're in.

- **2D mode is untouched**: same translucent-clear motion trails, pulsing diamond food, chunky eyes, grid — the classic game plays exactly as before.

- **2.5D mode**: the same 20×20 board rendered through a fixed perspective-tilted camera. Snake segments become low extruded neon boxes, grid lines and cells get depth shading (far rows fade toward black), and the board sits on a slab with a glowing cyan rim.

- **3D mode**: a full software-perspective 3D renderer written from scratch in canvas 2D — no THREE.js, no external dependencies, so `index.html` stays the sole entry point. It has an orbit camera ported from the reference game (drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, phi clamped above the board), camera-relative steering (arrow-up always means "away from you," snapped to the dominant board axis, exactly like the reference's `cameraForwardAxis` logic), tall glowing snake boxes with per-face shading and painter's-algorithm depth sorting, and billboard-projected food/power-ups.

- **Neon polish ported everywhere, especially 3D**: glowing floor-trail quads where the tail just vacated (replacing the 2D translucent-clear trick, which can't survive a moving camera), screen shake on crash, the red/white death flash, ghost-mode transparency pulse, world-space 3D particles that pop upward and bounce off the floor, pulsing pink food diamond, bobbing yuzu/star sprites with expiry blink — all rendered through the projection. The pixel-font HUD, slow-mo/ghost countdown badges, speed ramp, and P pause overlay are shared DOM/logic and work identically in every mode.

One design note: particles were refactored from pixel space into world space so a single particle system feeds all three renderers (the 2D view just maps world coordinates back to board pixels, with height shown as a slight upward lift).

## Summary

3D mode is now true volumetric 3D — the snake traverses a full 10×10×10 cube with real rise/dive moves, matching the movement and collision model of the original snake-game (`snake-logic.js`: unit-axis directions on x/y/z, no 180° reversals, tail-cell-safe-unless-growing, walls on all six faces). 2D and 2.5D are untouched — they still play on the classic 20×20 board with their original renderers.

**Gameplay in the volume**
- Every cell now carries a `z` layer. In 3D mode `dims()` returns a 10³ cube; food, power-ups, and free-cell lookups span the whole volume, and wall/self collisions check all three axes.
- Controls: arrows/WASD steer camera-relative on the current plane (as before), and **Q/Space rise, E/Shift dive** — real queued moves that obey the same no-180/no-dupe rules. A control-hint banner appears at the top of the frame when a 3D run starts and fades after ~5 seconds.
- Since the cube and the flat board are different worlds, switching between 3D and 2D/2.5D mid-run starts a fresh run in the new world (2D↔2.5D still switches live); the start-screen hint says so.

**Rendering the cube**
- Neon wireframe cage with a soft grid floor, drawn with the existing projection math; all 12 edges, the snake cubes, trail, food, power-ups, and particles go through one back-to-front depth sort, and brightness fades with camera distance.
- Depth cues: soft glowing floor shadows under every segment/food/power-up (fainter the higher the object), faint vertical drop-lines tying floaters to their shadows, a pulsing green ring around the cage at the head's layer, plus a "LAYER n/10" readout and an elevation gauge on the right edge.
- Camera: gentle auto-orbit (pauses while you drag), drag-to-orbit and scroll-to-zoom kept, with zoom limits retuned for the cube. Billboarded eyes now work for vertical travel too.

**All the juice survives in the volume**: glowing shrinking trail cubes, screen shake and red death-flash on crash, yuzu/star power-ups spawning anywhere in 3D with HUD countdowns, particles that bounce off the cube floor, pause overlay (now listing rise/dive keys), and the shared hi-score.

All changes are in. The game-over screen now presents an explicit choice instead of restarting on any input:

- **End screen buttons** — the game-over overlay keeps the score/hi-score/new-record display and now shows a neon-green "▶ PLAY AGAIN" button and a cyan "MAIN MENU" button, styled to match the arcade cabinet look.
- **Play Again** — calls the existing `startGame()`, which already rebuilds the snake, food, score, speed, and timers from scratch.
- **Main Menu** — a new `returnToMenu()` switches back to the title screen (with the INSERT COIN button and view-mode select) and wipes every piece of session state: snake, food, power-up, queued turns, particles, trail, slow-mo/ghost effects, screen shake, and score.
